item.title: Michigan basketball's Roddy Gayle Jr. can play after new court ruling
item.description: Another day, another win in court for Michigan basketball 's Roddy Gayle Jr. Gayle, a fifth-year wing, sat out the first two exhibition games of the season after an oversight in his ruling. He was cleared in September by a New York judge to compete with the Wolverines in 2026-27, but the preliminary injunction did not mention he participated in the NBA Summer League, even though it was known to all parties. This week, Gayle's legal team filed an amended complaint in his case with the Supreme Court of the State of New York. It prevents the NCAA from declaring Gayle ineligible "on the basis of Plaintiff's participation in the 2026 NBA Summer League, his receipt of a $1,700 Summer League stipend, or his agent agreement," per court documents . The action has been granted for now , which should put Gayle on track to play Sunday, Oct. 25, in Michigan's final exhibition game against Houston in Grand Rapids at Van Andel Arena (1 p.m., BTN+). [ MUST WATCH: Make "Hail Yes!" your go-to Wolverines podcast, available anywhere you listen to podcasts ( Apple , Spotify ) or watch live/on demand on YouTube . ] "His injunction order didn't address his participation in Summer League. Simple as that," coach Mike Boynton Jr. said Oct. 11 after Gayle missed U-M's 87-62 exhibition win over Eastern Michigan. "There needs to be an amendment added to the injunction that says this includes not having anything to do with his participation in Summer League, which we hope will be in the next couple days." This does not mean Gayle's situation is fully resolved as the NCAA can still file an appeal in the coming weeks. However, U-M is clear from the NCAA "assessing or threatening to assess any penalty" for playing Gayle in upcoming games. Gayle, a Niagara Falls native, played a career-high 39 games last season for the national champions, averaging 7.3 points, 3.3 rebounds and 1.3 assists in 21.1 minutes per game that included a key 16-point performance against Alabama in the Sweet 16. He has played in 146 games across his career, starting 72 games (including 25 for U-M in 2025-26). "I did not leave college for professional basketball," Gayle said in a statement when he filed his original lawsuit. "I completed four seasons, I graduated, and the NCAA’s new carve-out told me I could not play a fifth. Only then did I turn to professional basketball. "I have never played in a professional regular-season game, and I have never been paid a salary to play basketball, in any league or any country. … I am not asking the court to order any school to put me on its roster. I am not asking the NCAA for money, and I seek no damages. I am asking only that the NCAA be restrained from declaring me ineligible, from interfering with Michigan’s decision to let me play, and from punishing Michigan, its coaches, or my teammates for following this court’s order, so that I may compete for a spot on the same terms as every other player.” Tony Garcia is the Michigan beat writer for the Detroit Free Press.

But to do it, while chasing and with the conviction that he has done it, right from the get go he was very sure, played lovely shots in the powerplay, showed good intent. But the intent never dropped, it just kept almost going up. "And with Shubman Gill you always knew that talent was there, he had a very good calm head and in terms of pure shot making skills he was right up there and with IPL being such a high pressure tournament and you need to constantly be up with the strike rate and run rate. I think people are just learning to play newer shots, more attacking shots and are becoming more fearless day by day.” Is the Dinesh Karthik backlash fair? Social media reduces everything to a comparison, so it is not surprising that two posts placed next to each other look damaging. On the evidence supplied, however, a single “Is this good to watch?” tweet written mid-chase does not prove that Karthik wanted to belittle Gill. It could just as easily be read as a comment on how one-sided the contest had become, and the emojis suggest awe more than disapproval. Even so, fans have a point about tone. Karthik’s post about Brook was celebratory and direct, while his earlier message about Gill carried a question mark that many read as sceptical, and perception counts for a lot when the subject is an Indian player. His longer remarks on Cricbuzz were warm and detailed, and any honest summary of the story has to include them. The claims of jealousy and a KKR-era rivalry are another matter, since no one has presented proof, and they say more about the mood of the fanbase than about Karthik. A broadcaster in his position is free to give opinions, but he should expect his words to be weighed against each other. The simplest advice for commentators is consistency. If the praise is the same for every batter, nobody can build a story about favourites. item.title: Bruno Fernandes’ £4m Cheshire home burgled during Manchester United defeat to Como
item.description: Bruno Fernandes’ £4m Cheshire home burgled during Manchester United defeat to Como Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes’ £4 million home in Cheshire was burgled during the 4-1 Champions League defeat to Como on Wednesday night, the Daily Mail reports. The Portuguese midfielder’s six-bedroom mansion in Nether Alderley was targeted around 8.30pm while he played in United’s heavy defeat. The police are already investigating the incident, and officers are working to identify those responsible. According to reports, three masked men entered the luxury property and stole several items, including designer jewellery. Fernandes’ family were not at home when the burglary took place, and the suspects are believed to have spent only about five minutes inside the house. Neighbours reportedly spotted three unknown men in the garden of a nearby property and alerted the police. However, when officers arrived, the suspects had already dispersed. Cheshire Police confirmed officers were called to the Alderley Park area of Nether Alderley around 8.30pm after reports of suspicious activity. A police spokesperson said: “At around 8.30pm on Wednesday 21 October, police were called to reports of suspicious activity at an address in the Alderley Park area of Nether Alderley. “The caller reported three unknown men in the rear garden of a neighbouring property. Officers attended the scene, and on arrival there was no trace of the suspects. “However, officers discovered that there had been a burglary at the address and a number of items had been stolen.” Detective Inspector David Jarvis added: “This investigation is in its early stages at this time, and we’re committed to doing all we can to trace the people responsible. “As part of our enquiries, we’re keen to hear from anyone who was in the local area at the time and believes they may have witnessed anything suspicious.” Fernandes was in Italy when the break-in occurred, having travelled with United for their Champions League fixture against Como . The midfielder played 67 minutes before being replaced by Joshua Zirkzee in a disappointing night for Michael Carrick’s side. United are supporting their captain and have asked for privacy for him and his family as they deal with the incident.

item.title: ‘You step in the game’ – Barcelona star hits back at fans after PSG criticism
item.description: ‘You step in the game’ – Barcelona star hits back at fans after PSG criticism Barcelona star João Cancelo has taken to social media on Thursday, to launch a defence of his most recent performance. Defender Cancelo was for his part in from the off on Tuesday night, as Barcelona made the trip to Paris for a Champions League showdown with Luis Enrique’s PSG. En route to a first defeat of the season for the visitors, however, the Portuguese was singled out for heavy criticism. Much of the condemnation came courtesy of those of a Blaugrana persuasion, frustrated with Cancelo’s shortcomings on the defensive side of the ball. As alluded to above, though, the former Manchester City man is evidently not ready to take such backlash without defending his name. Taking to his official Instagram account on Thursday, Cancelo hit back at his critics, writing: ‘From the stands, everyone’s an expert. I want to see them step into the game and handle the pressure.’ Conor Laird – GSFN

Chase Brown Oct 11, 2026; Miami Gardens, Florida, USA; Cincinnati Bengals halfback Chase Brown (30) runs with the ball against the Miami Dolphins during the second quarter at Hard Rock Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Brown in PPR fantasy formats currently ranks as RB20 and is coming off his most discouraging game of the season, in Week 5 against the Miami Dolphins. item.title: Bruno Fernandes’ house targeted by robbers while playing for Man Utd in Champions League
item.description: Manchester United are offering full support to Bruno Fernandes and his family after a burglary at his home while he was playing in a Champions league clash against Como on Wednesday evening. A damaging evening in Lombardy saw United fall to a heavy 4-1 defeat against Cesc Fabregas’ side, lengthening their winless streak to seven matches and prompting Fernandes to openly criticise the tactics of boss Michael Carrick . Having flown back from Italy alongside his teammates early on Thursday morning, the Portuguese international was forced to handle the fallout from the break-in that occurred during his time abroad. It is understood that Fernandes’ family were not present when the incident occurred, with officers attending promptly and United giving full assistance to their skipper. Fernandes, meanwhile, is set to escape internal punishment after the Manchester United captain’s outburst in Como. The defeat and Fernandes' statements intensified scrutiny over Carrick’s position prior to Sunday’s Premier League match against Bournemouth, but it is understood he will remain in his post . United skipper Fernandes has been a pale imitation of last season’s performer so far this term, and questioned Carrick’s tactics as another Champions League trip ended with an eye-catching post-match player interview following on from last week’s remarks by Lisandro Martinez. Bruno Fernandes questioned Michael Carrick’s tactics after the Como defeat (PA) Fernandes claimed it was the staff’s decision “not to press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little bit of space in behind” in Como. Captain Fernandes, who was substituted after 67 minutes at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia, delivered a damning assessment after the game. He told TNT Sports: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little bit of space in behind, and trying to get the ball in the first moment, to wait for them, to give them the ball. “Sometimes when you give too much of the ball to these teams, they get confidence. They have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people get frustrated, and then obviously when you recover the ball, the legs and the brain are much more difficult to make it work.” Asked further about the tactics, he said: “It’s on the manager and on the staff to say it, it is not on me. “I just said that I think sometimes we have to be more brave under pressure, trying to take a risk of getting that press very high and making them uncomfortable, as they did to us.” Yet, the Press Association understands United are not expected to punish Fernandes for his impassioned post-match interview a week on from Martinez’s caustic remarks, which led to a fine and talks with the club hierarchy.

item.description: Seahawks get terrible Elijah Arroyo news ahead of Week 7 Chiefs game originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Seattle Seahawks got two major pieces of injury news on Thursday before the team's Week 7 matchup against the undefeated Kansas City Chiefs . One piece of news was good, and the other was about as bad as it gets. While running back Zach Charbonnet was confirmed to have been activated off the physically unable to perform list, the Seahawks got some terrible news on their highly-drafted tight end. According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , the Seahawks are going to lose Elijah Arroyo for the rest of the 2026 NFL season, as he's having season-ending shoulder surgery on Thursday, ending his second NFL season before it could really even begin. Elijah Arroyo to have season-ending shoulder surgery "Source: Seahawks TE Elijah Arroyo is undergoing shoulder surgery today and will miss the rest of the season," Schefter reports. This is a brutal blow for the Seahawks' second-year tight end. This was set to be a year where he'd see an increase in involvement in the offense, but now, before he could really get anything going, his season is over. The 23-year-old tight end caught 15 of 26 targets for 179 yards and one touchdown last season during the Seahawks' Super Bowl run. In 2026, Arroyo has caught just one of his two targets for 17 yards with no touchdowns, and now will miss the rest of the regular season. MORE : ESPN analyst proposes Eagles trade Saquon Barkley to Texans for very intriguing haul After four receptions for 86 yards and a touchdown during the preseason, Arroyo sparked some optimism heading into his second NFL season after being drafted in the second round of the 2025 NFL Draft. Now, with this report from Schefter coming out on Thursday, his sophomore season is over. Seattle will continue to rely on AJ Barner as their top tight end this season, with Erid Saubert and Nick Kallerup filling out the depth chart as Arroyo misses time. Tight end might be a trade target for the Seahawks this Fall if they can improve on their 3-3 record by the NFL trade deadline in November. But for now, the Seahawks are down a young tight end who would've been a nice pass-catcher in this offense. Arroyo is out for the year and will look to come back in 2027. Deco impressed by Busquets’ tactical understanding and personality Busquets has begun his coaching career with Barcelona’s reserve side, working as an assistant to Juliano Belletti . His initial weeks in the role have reportedly given the club further reason to believe he could develop into a high-level coach. Deco was particularly impressed during a meeting with the former midfielder , according to the report. Busquets is said to have demonstrated a deep understanding of football, a clear tactical vision and a strong personality, alongside an intimate knowledge of Barça’s philosophy and playing style. Busquets is currently working as Belletti’s assistant with Barça Atletic. They were hampered by the dew, another factor in Sri Lanka's decision to bat second. England made mistakes in the field and their bowlers struggled to grip the ball. item.title: Trump accuses LeBron James of disrespecting US anthem, demands apology
item.description: LeBron James [NBAE via Getty Images] US President Donald Trump has accused basketball star LeBron James of disrespecting the US by not being still while the national anthem was sung. James, who now plays for the Philadelphia 76ers, appeared to be practising a golf swing and basketball shots as the anthem was being performed ahead of the season opening match against the New York Knicks on Wednesday. "While listening to our National Anthem, LeBron James disrespects our Country!," Trump posted on social media. "LeBron James should apologize to all of those Great American Warriors and Heroes who died for the American Flag." James has not responded to the president's latest comments but the pair have criticised each other in the past. "I said right from the beginning that he's no good, a TOTAL DISGRACE," Trump added referring to James. In July, when asked to choose between James and Michael Jordan as the all-time greatest basketball player in history, Trump said he preferred Jordan and suggested James, who is black, might be "a racist". "I only like people that like me," Trump said.

item.title: Revisiting Colorado's historic 2024 shutout win over Oklahoma State
item.description: The Colorado Buffaloes delivered a commanding performance in their most recent meeting with Oklahoma State , rolling to a 52-0 victory at Folsom Field on Nov. 29, 2024. For this Throwback Thursday, that regular-season finale takes the spotlight as Colorado prepares to face the Cowboys again Saturday . No. 23 Colorado improved to 9-3 overall and 7-2 in the Big 12 behind Shedeur Sanders ’ five touchdown passes and Travis Hunter ’s three touchdown receptions. The defense forced four turnovers and only allowed 147 total yards, giving Colorado its first shutout since 2021. Hunter and Sanders put on a show Sanders completed 34 of 41 passes for 438 yards, with one interception. Hunter caught 10 passes for 116 yards and added an interception on defense, solidifying his Heisman Trophy candidacy. “Travis clinched the Heisman today with his performance,” coach Deion Sanders said afterward. LaJohntay Wester finished with 11 receptions for 175 yards and two touchdowns, including a 69-yard score early in the third quarter. DJ McKinney added a 13-yard interception return for a touchdown as Oklahoma State finished 3-9 overall and winless in conference play. Honorable mention: McCartney’s 1991 gamble Colorado’s Nov. 9, 1991 visit to Stillwater produced a thrilling finish against a winless Cowboys team. Trailing 12-10 with 14 seconds remaining, No. 14 Colorado lined up for a 36-yard field goal. After Oklahoma State called a timeout, coach Bill McCartney called for a fake. Holder Robbie James found freshman tight end Christian Fauria for a 20-yard touchdown with six seconds left, giving Colorado a 16-12 win. Colorado finished 6-0-1 in conference play and shared the Big Eight championship with Nebraska. After the game, Oklahoma State head coach Pat Jones said, "The play at the end, however long I've been coaching, is the gutsiest call I've ever seen." item.title: Maatsen, Cash And Kamara To Start | 4-2-3-1 Aston Villa Predicted Lineup Vs Manchester City
item.description: Maatsen, Cash And Kamara To Start | 4-2-3-1 Aston Villa Predicted Lineup Vs Manchester City Aston Villa will entertain Manchester City at Villa Park this Saturday as they look to secure a good result at home in the Premier League. The Villans managed to earn an impressive 3-1 win over Viking recently, which should give them a lot of confidence going into this game. Unai Emery will stick with his favoured 4-2-3-1 formation and is expected to make some changes to his first XI for this game. Ian Maatsen, Matty Cash and Boubacar Kamara could all play from the start of this clash. 4-2-3-1 Aston Villa Predicted Lineup To Face Manchester City Defence Zion Suzuki will function in between the sticks for the Villans after conceding one goal in his last outing. Victor Lindelof will continue to play alongside Pau Torres at the centre of the Aston Villa backline as they look to keep the opposition at bay during the 90 minutes. Matty Cash will try to prove his worth as the right-back, while Ian Maatsen fills in on the other side as the left-back. Both of them will have to pick and choose their moments to join in on the attack. Taylor Harwood-Bellis and Tyrone Mings will offer cover for the defensive positions on the bench. BIRMINGHAM, ENGLAND – OCTOBER 21: Emi Buendia of Aston Villa scores a penalty for his team’s second goal during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between Aston Villa FC and Viking FK at Villa Park on October 21, 2026 in Birmingham, England. (Photo by Richard Heathcote/Getty Images) Midfield Boubacar Kamara and Joao Gomes will anchor the midfield for the Villans as they focus on making life tough for the opposition at the centre of the park and engineering some decent chances in the final third. The talented trio of Ibrahim Mbaye, Emiliano Buendia and John McGinn will operate just ahead of them as part of Emery’s attack. All three of them need to link up with each other well if the Villans are to cause some problems for the opposition defenders this Saturday. Leon Goretzka and Alejandro Garnacho will have to be content with a spot on the bench and might come on to influence the game in the second 45 minutes if required. Attack Nicolas Jackson will spearhead Emery’s attack in the final third. He would be eager to get his name on the scoresheet after failing to do so against Viking earlier this week. Tammy Abraham will be available for selection on the bench as he waits for his chance to shine in the final quarter of the game if required.

item.title: WWE’s Cody Rhodes gives fresh timeline on retirement after signing ‘last contract’
item.description: WWE’s Cody Rhodes gives fresh timeline on retirement after signing ‘last contract’ appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . In the next decade, Cody Rhodes will retire from professional wrestling after signing his latest contract with WWE , which will be his “last” one. Speaking to Chris Van Vliet, the “American Nightmare” gave an update on the timeline for his retirement. He previously told Van Vliet that he was going to retire at 40. Rhodes, who is now 41, reinforced that the latest contract he signed will be his “last.” However, it will “go for a while.” If all goes well, he plans to retire within the next six or seven years. “With all that said, my time with WWE could go probably seven years, six [or] seven [years],” he said, before saying he didn’t mean to make a “6-7” joke. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Cody Rhodes reveals that he only wants to wrestle for another 6–7 years. He also reveals that the new contract he recently signed with WWE will be his last. (Insight with @ChrisVanVliet ) pic.twitter.com/qOA26NBmV2 — SuplexInsider (@SuplexInsider) October 22, 2026 Now, his timeline is rough. He doesn’t want his retirement timeline to be set in stone quite yet, but what’s most important is that he doesn’t “overstay my welcome.” He definitely doesn’t want to wrestle into his 50s, like legends such as Rey Mysterio are currently doing. Rhodes has been given so much from the industry, but he also knows it’s almost his time to “stop taking” from it. When will Cody Rhodes retire from WWE? Joe Camporeale-Imagn Images. It sounds like Rhodes will retire from WWE within the next decade, so fans should buckle up. He is still at the top of the company, but he seems to understand that Father Time is undefeated. Some of his decision to hang it up might depend on his success in Hollywood. After having a small role in the Liam Neeson-led Naked Gun reboot, he starred in the Street Fighter movie alongside his former WWE rival, Roman Reigns. The movie has been a hit so far, grossing over $50 million to date. It topped the domestic box office with its $31.1 million haul during its opening weekend. item.title: Last-minute addition wins Billy Horschel Invitational on APGA Tour
item.description: Enrique Dimayuga, a last-minute addition to the field at the Billy Horschel Invitational Presented by Cisco on the Advocates Professional Golf Association Tour, made the most of his opportunity. The event had just a 21-man field and Dimayuga got in as the first alternate and hustled to get to the golf course. “I was over the moon,” Dimayuga said. “I really didn’t have anything planned for this week. I said, ‘I’m going to book my flight straight away and get on over here.’” The APGA Tour rookie, born in the Philippines and raised in London, earned his first professional victory with a 9-under 135 score in the 36-hole event at the Evermore Resort’s Grand Cypress Course in Orlando. “It feels great,” Dimayuga said. “Definitely, trying to win is a skill. Having done that at different levels, and the competition just keeps going up and up and up as you go into the professional ranks. To start here is great. There was a lot of nerves overnight, sleeping on the lead and being in a position where there was lots of people behind me. I’m very, very glad to be able to get the job done. Proud of the way I played. A really grateful moment.” Dimayuga, who finished his college golf career at SMU last year, banked $30,000 from the tournament's $100,000 total prize fund. Dimayuga can probably send a thank you card to Joey Stills, who withdrew in order to compete in PGA Tour Q School First Stage, allowing Dimayuga to get in the APGA event. “It means everything, you know, opportunities to get in high-level golf tournaments. I was just very grateful,” Dimayuga said. “It’s also a great learning experience to play in an invitational as well where it’s only the best players on this tour to be playing this week.” This article originally appeared on Golfweek: Last-minute addition wins Billy Horschel Invitational on APGA Tour

There's still a long way to go, and many teams still have an opportunity to prove themselves to be taken seriously, especially Michigan *. So, just how will Week 8 look as we go? Our writers take turns picking all the games in the League straight up and against the spread for your wagering and reading consumption — do with it as you wish. As a reminder, if there’s an asterisk next to the pick, that means the team will win, but not cover. If there is a tie, rather than have a cage match or old-fashioned duel, we’ll settle it with less violence and go with the tried-and-true coin flip, where George Washington has the say. item.title: Ravens’ Cam Jurgens has just 1 big question after Eagles traded him in concussion protocol
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Ravens’ Cam Jurgens has just 1 big question after Eagles traded him in concussion protocol appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Baltimore Ravens need to get back on track in Week 7. Baltimore lost an ugly divisional game with Cleveland 13-10 last weekend, moving them to 4-2 on the season. Hopefully the Ravens will get a boost this weekend by finally getting one of their newest players on the field. Ravens center Cam Jurgens shared one interesting question about his trade in a recent interview. “It’s been a wild process,” Jurgens said, per Clifton Brown and Ryan Mink from the team’s official website. “Has anybody been traded while they’re in the concussion protocol? It just feels so good to be out of this protocol and start to feel a little bit like myself again. I love it here, enjoying it. Anytime you get traded it’s such a crazy, whirlwind experience. But this is such a good organization. I’m happy, excited to be here.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Jurgens was in the middle of concussion protocol when his trade was finalized. It turns out that Baltimore did perform their due diligence on Jurgens before the trade. The Ravens quietly sent two team doctors to the Eagles training facility to examine Jurgens. There they performed the same type of physical that Maxx Crosby did not pass earlier this offseason. Jurgens has yet to play a game for Baltimore since that trade was finalized. Fortunately, he is expected to make his Ravens debut in Week 7 on Sunday. Jurgens was a full participant in practice on Wednesday. The debut of Jurgens will allow rookie Vega Ioane to move back to right guard. This new Ravens offensive time may need some time to come together, at least on the right side. But once that happens, Baltimore should be even more powerful in the trenches. It will be exciting to see how Jurgens looks during his debut this weekend. Next up for the Ravens is a home game against the Bengals. That AFC North clash kicks off at 1 p.m. ET on Oct. 25 from M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore. item.title: Juventus CEO expresses support for manager Luciano Spalletti
item.description: Juventus CEO expresses support for manager Luciano Spalletti Serie A side Juventus haven’t had smooth sailing in Serie A in recent weeks. They picked up a hefty 3-0 loss to Lazio at the weekend and this came days after a 1-1 draw against Cagliari. Despite that, Luciano Spalletti retains the backing of the club. The Bianconeri, as things stand, are 2-1 down to Rennes in their third game of the Europa League. CEO Giovanni Carnevali spoke to Sky Italia about the club’s situation and he was specifically quizzed about their backing of Spalletti, amidst the recent run of poor results. He said – via Calciomercato : “We have to try to rebuild. In recent years, there have been mistakes, not only sportingly but also financially.” “We find ourselves in this settlement agreement situation that has left us stuck in many situations. We have to try to rebuild, provide continuity, and not change every moment, otherwise we’ll always start from scratch.” Carnevali declared that every period of struggle shouldn’t end with a managerial change and Juventus do not want to do that again. He said: “I’ve been here for four months and I bring my ideas. I don’t think it’s right to change every time there’s a problem. The Juventus shirt weighs on you, and that doesn’t give the right peace of mind to work, especially for the young players. They’re young, we have to support them, and we have extraordinary fans. We have to bring joy, but we know it takes time, not haste.” Carnevali was also asked about whether the pressure of managing Juve is sometimes too much for managers. The Italian responded: “The manager is always the same. He knows he has to work. It’s true, the shirt is heavy and the bench is hot, but he’s part of a big club like Juve. Here, maybe you don’t have a couple of good games and there’s already talk of changes, but it doesn’t affect us that much. We know what we have to do, the manager knows what needs to be done and the critical issues.” Kaustubh Pandey – GIFN

item.title: Could Canadiens' key injury create opportunity for Red Wings, Larkin?
item.description: VANCOUVER, Canada — There's one team, apparently not on Dylan Larkin's list of teams he'd accept a trade to, who desperately need Larkin, or a player like him. The Montreal Canadiens have been a good fit from the day Larkin asked for a trade from the Red Wings in early June and remain so, now. Even more, now, as their No. 1 center, Nick Suzuki, is out two to four weeks with an upper-body injury. Suzuki appeared to hurt himself Tuesday, Oct. 20, injuring a hand after attempting to block a shot. More: Ron Duguay, former Red Wings forward, dies at age 69 Larkin reportedly has a list of 10 teams he'd agree to be traded, but Montreal never has appeared on the list. Interestingly, it's the Canadiens who are one of the few teams in the NHL who both have the type of young veteran players, and/or prospects that would entice the Wings to make a trade, and also have the salary cap space. But, again, Larkin doesn't appear motivated to play in Montreal. Can the Suzuki injury change things in any way? More: Carter Mazur's role grows as he adjusts to NHL life with Red Wings Montreal made it to the Eastern Conference Finals last season and could do so again this spring. But a ragged start (4-3-2), combined with the Suzuki injury and several players slumping, have made the situation a bit uneven to begin the season. Acquiring Larkin would be a significant Band-Aid to a lot of ills in Montreal. In fact, fans at the Oct. 10 game in Montreal when the Wings visited serenaded Larkin with "we want Larkin" chants from the first period onward to show their desire to have Larkin in the Canadiens' lineup. "It was interesting," Larkin said after the game. "I never would have imagined that in this building in my career, but they're passionate fans." tkulfan@detroitnews.com @tkulfan This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Could Canadiens' key injury create opportunity for Red Wings, Larkin?

item.description: Denny Medley-Imagn Images Chiefs O-lineman Josh Simmons’ back injury update is a real bad sign for career appeared first on ClutchPoints . The Kansas City Chiefs have gotten off to a strong start to the 2026 NFL season, currently sitting at 5-0 following their recent home win over the Los Angeles Chargers . The Chiefs have played this entire season without starting offensive lineman Josh Simmons , whom the team selected in the first round of the 2025 NFL Draft. Now, the team has gotten a worrisome injury update on Simmons as the season progresses. “Chiefs head athletic trainer Rick Burkholder says the team feels like LT Josh Simmons has plateaued in his improvement with his back injury. Simmons consulted with his family yesterday to figure out next steps, which is why he missed practice for personal reasons. Burkholder says Simmons has decided to go on injured reserve,” reported Jesse Newell of The Athletic on X, formerly Twitter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Nate Taylor of ESPN also reported that “Rick Burkholder said Josh Simmons still doesn’t need surgery as part of his rehab & recovery from the bulging, herniated disc.” Back injuries are certainly not something to mess around with, so it’s no surprise to see Simmons and the Chief being particularly cautious in his return process. “It was higher up than what we see in most of our offensive linemen,” Burkholder said of Simmons’ MRI, per Taylor. The Chiefs’ offensive line has been performing relatively well so far this year despite Simmons’ absence, paving the way for Kenneth Walker III to look like one of the best running backs in the league so far this season. item.title: Is there bad blood between Hendrickson, Bengals? What ex-Bengal said
item.description: Former Bengals defensive end Trey Hendrickson was asked what he would say to those who suggest there was bad blood when he left Cincinnati as he and the Baltimore Ravens prepare to host their AFC North rival in NFL Week 7 at M&T Bank Stadium. "As a Christian, I forgive and obviously I move on," Hendrickson said . "And there's some wonderful times that I had there. Like I said, there'll be a time to reflect and all that stuff. But right now, there's an opponent in front of us. And as the Ravens, we look forward to capitalizing on everything that we can this week." Earlier in the week, Ravens linebacker Trenton Simpson told reporters he's predicting a multi-sack game for Hendrickson against his former team. Hendrickson, who played five seasons for the Bengals and led the NFL in sacks in 2024 , has totaled two sacks in the four games in which he's played for the Ravens this season. He missed two games because of finger surgery. "(Facing Hendrickson will) be fun. It'll be fun," Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow said after practice Oct. 21. "I got to practice with him for a long time, and I'm sure he's excited to hit me a little bit after not hitting me for so long. Yeah, it'll be fun." "He's a good player," Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said of Hendrickson earlier in the week, per The Enquirer's Pat Brennan . "They got a lot of good players in their defense, and we got to put together a great plan and be able to execute it to give ourselves the best chance to win." item.title: Cam Skattebo And AJ Brown Headline Our Week 7 Fantasy Football Buy-Low Trade Targets
item.description: New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo (44) celebrates after the game against the Arizona Cardinals at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect When a fantasy star is struggling, their fantasy football owner could panic and sell that player at a discount. That's when you need to swoop in, recognize the value, and make your move. These are the fantasy football players you should be buying low on heading into Week 7. RB Cam Skattebo, New York Giants Skattebo was punished in Week 6 for fumbling a win away in Week 5. He played six snaps and didn't see a single touch in a loss to the New Orleans Saints. However, the rushing attack struggled mightily without him, and the Giants desperately need to win as they attempt to win a weak NFC East. We wouldn't be surprised if Skattebo stepped right back in as the lead back in Week 7 after his punishment. This doesn't come with risk, but the upside makes it worth it. You could be getting a fringe RB1 for pennies on the dollar. Just understand, his volume is not guaranteed, and another fumble could spell disaster for his fantasy outlook. RB Chase Brown, Cincinnati Bengals The last time we saw Brown on the field was back in Week 5. It was not a good day for the Bengals' starter. He saw his touches reduced after fumbling, and backup Samaje Perine outperformed him. Brown finished the game with 13 carries for just 30 yards at 3.0 yards per carry, while Perine saw 14 carries, which he turned into 68 yards at 4.9 yards per carry, while also adding a touchdown through the air. While that's concerning, we view it as a blip on the radar. We are not anticipating a 10th-year breakout from a 31-year-old career backup. Go get Brown before he bounces back on Sunday. WR AJ Brown, New England Patriots Brown played one of the worst games of his career when he returned to action in Week 6. We are writing this off as rust in his first game back. There is a career's worth of sample size telling us that he's a great receiver. He didn't suddenly forget how to catch the ball. More importantly, he was getting open and saw 10 targets. He also looked like he was moving well coming off of his ankle injury. If his fantasy owner is panicking, make an offer and go get him. Move quickly because he plays tonight on Thursday Night Football. You'll be acquiring a league-winner. WR Michael Wilson, Arizona Cardinals Wilson looked like a fantasy superstar early in the season, but has oddly fallen off a cliff since Marvin Harrison Jr was traded. Kendrick Bourne has stepped up as the team's WR1 since the move. We have seen Bourne have these stretches before, and it never lasts very long. We are confident that Wilson re-emerges as the clear-cut WR1 in Arizona, which is a role he has already proven he can turn into fantasy WR1 production consistently. Sports Business Journal (via Pro Football Talk) reports that his alt cast—which aired on ESPN— only garnered 351,000 viewers . item.title: Penta Reveals His MITB Cash-In Plans
item.description: WWE Penta claimed one of the biggest victories of his WWE career this year. He outlasted five other competitors in the 2026 Men’s Money in the Bank ladder match and climbed to the top to grab the coveted briefcase. In a recent appearance on the Busted Open Radio , Penta said that he felt he had the power in his hands and revealed that he would cash in the Money in the Bank contract when he felt in his soul that the time had come to do it. Moreover, the masked luchador also stated that he started thinking about his cash-in, name-dropping the reigning World Champions, Roman Reigns and Sami Zayn. “But, as for a briefcase, I actually feel like that. I have the f***ing power in my hands basically because at one time, I don’t know where, I don’t know when, but when I feel it in my soul that it is the perfect time for a cash-in, I will. Now, I started thinking something, Roman, you know Sami. I don’t know because it’s my first time but at the same time, I want to do the best, forget the world champions, you know? But for now, I enjoy every presentation with my briefcase, with fire, everything involving about it. I enjoy it.” Penta signed with WWE in 2025 and has been a captivating fixture since his debut on RAW. The year 2026 has been a breakout year for the former AEW star. He won his first-ever singles WWE title in March 2026. Following that, Penta earned the opportunity to challenge Roman Reigns for the World Heavyweight title on RAW in Mexico City. Despite not winning the bout, he was widely applauded for his in-ring performance and marked a major shift in his career, leading to his Money in the Bank victory. With Penta revealing his mindset regarding the Money in the Bank cash-in, it will be exciting to witness whether he is successful and earns his first-ever World Championship. That trajectory centers around true freshman quarterback Tait Reynolds. While Reynolds has not immediately hit the ground running as an explosive passer, he has already guided Clemson to three victories as a starter, including two within Atlantic Coast Conference play. Through that trial and error, Morris sees specific mental and physical traits that could ultimately elevate Reynolds into one of college football’s premier signal-callers. While an unflappable mindset helps erase the anxiety of upcoming possessions, Morris often has to pull back the reins to ensure the young quarterback diagnoses what went wrong. “Some guys get down after a bad play; he’s not that guy,” he said. “He’s quick to flush it. item.title: Seahawks make exciting Zach Charbonnet roster move for Week 7 vs. Chiefs
item.description: Seahawks make exciting Zach Charbonnet roster move for Week 7 vs. Chiefs originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Seattle Seahawks , through the first six weeks of the 2026 NFL season, have had a running back problem. Jadarian Price has been disappointing, and he's on injured reserve right now. Emmanuel Wilson and George Holani haven't really impressed either. They've held down the fort as Seattle's gotten off to a 3-3 record, but with the team now set to face the Kansas City Chiefs in primetime for Kenneth Walker III's first game against his former team, the Seahawks got some good news on their backfield. Ian Rapoport of NFL Network is reporting that the Seahawks are activating RB Zach Charbonnet off the PUP list, bringing him back for Week 7 and giving him a chance to suit up to help the shaky Seattle backfield when they go up against Walker this week. Seahawks get good news as Zach Charbonnet activated off PUP "The Seahawks have activated RB Zach Charbonnet from the PUP list, a significant move," Rapoport reported Thursday. This is a significant move for the Seahawks indeed, as getting Charbonnet back to a backfield that has severely underwhelmed to begin the season is huge news. It's especially great timing with Walker on the other side of the game this week, as their Super Bowl MVP has been a true superstar for the Chiefs this season. While Wilson and Holani have had their nice moments through the first six weeks of the season, the Seahawks backfield is in dire need of a true star to lead the way. MORE : ESPN analyst proposes Eagles trade Saquon Barkley to Texans for very intriguing haul Charbonnet can be just that for the Seahawks, and with this news that he's been activated off the PUP list, he might finally be back in action Sunday against the Chiefs. But it's still worth noting that he's coming off a serious injury late last season and might not be at 100% strength just yet. He isn't even a lock to play in Week 7, as just because he's been activated doesn't mean he'll play. Seattle had to activate him on Thursday, so this move was expected. Still, it's a great sign that Charbonnet is off the PUP list and completely on the Seahawks' 53-man roster. With a matchup against the Chiefs and Walker on tap on Sunday night, this is some very timely news for the Seahawks with their RB1 coming back this season. item.title: Former Texas high school football star cut by Tennessee Titans after reported gun incident
item.description: Tennessee Titans defensive tackle Jordan Elliott (95) arrives for an NFL football game against the Houston Texans in Nashville, Tenn., Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026. (AP Photo/John Amis) (John Amis/Associated Press) A former Texas high school football standout was released by the Tennessee Titans after reportedly retrieving a gun during a dispute with a teammate at the team's practice facility. Jordan Elliott, 28, a former Houston Westside High School star, was released Tuesday following an Oct. 15 incident involving offensive tackle JC Latham, according to Texas HS Football. The dispute reportedly began during practice, when Elliott and Latham had a heated confrontation. Elliott was told to leave the field. After removing his pads, he headed toward the players' parking area. Elliott went to retrieve a firearm from his vehicle before veteran defensive lineman John Franklin-Myers intervened and helped de-escalate the situation, according to multiple reports cited by Texas HS Football. No one was injured. ALSO READ: Watch: Cowboys insider wonders if Brian Schottenheimer is on hot seat ahead of Eagles game Titans coach Robert Saleh confirmed Wednesday that a gun was involved, calling Elliott's actions a serious lapse in judgment. Saleh also voiced support for the defensive lineman, saying the incident should not define his NFL career. The NFL is reviewing the incident. Elliott grew up in Missouri City and became one of the nation's top defensive line recruits at Houston's Westside High School. During his junior season, he recorded 78 tackles, 31 tackles for loss and 12 sacks, earning first-team Class 6A All-State honors from the Associated Press. He initially signed with the University of Texas before transferring to Missouri, where he earned first-team All-SEC honors. The Cleveland Browns selected him in the third round of the 2020 NFL Draft, with the 88th overall pick. Elliott signed a two-year, $8 million contract with Tennessee during the offseason after spending two seasons with the San Francisco 49ers. He appeared in five games for the Titans before his release and has played in 102 NFL games during his career. Subscribe There’s more to San Antonio with the Express-News. item.title: Haiti move Nations League home clash with USA to Miami amid gang violence crisis
item.description: Concacaf approves exceptional hosting arrangement Haiti to face US in South Florida on 14 November Miami’s Haitian community offers home advantage On Thursday, Concacaf announced that it had approved Haiti’s request to relocate their Nations League quarter-final first leg on 14 November from Kingston, Jamaica, to Miami in an “exceptional hosting arrangement”. Haiti have been unable to play nominal “home” games within their borders since July 2021, with the United Nations estimating that 90% of Port-au-Prince – including the national stadium – is controlled by violent gangs. Initially, Haiti’s match, the first leg of a home-and-away series against the United States, had been booked in Kingston. The Grenadiers had previously played their World Cup qualifiers in Curaçao, Aruba and Barbados. However, the Nations League format slated Curaçao and Jamaica to host their matches on the same night as Haiti’s, shunting Haiti to Sabina Park, the home of the Jamaica national team until their current venue opened in 1962. Now a cricket ground, Sabina Park hosted two of Haiti’s Nations League qualifiers. Continue reading...

Any chance the Independent Football Regulator could also force the sale of Manchester United while it is at it? – James Marriott. item.title: Trump’s Fifa peace prize was a sham. A reimagined award can still have meaning | Leander Schaerlaeckens
item.description: The first awarding marked the apex of Gianni Infantino’s hubris. A new version could highlight the good in the world of soccer Sign up for our free newsletter here Poor Fifa peace prize. Unloved, unliked, mocked, tainted by association with its first winner. And now demoted, too, after Fifa’s president, Gianni Infantino, dumped the thing on the global governing body’s “social responsibility committee” to look after. To redeem it, rather than to ditch it, to spare Infantino the embarrassment of acknowledging that his fake prize was really just a fake prize all along. Here is where we should probably acknowledge that, as fake prizes go, and in the context of what it was intended to accomplish, the first awarding of the Fifa peace prize was an unqualified success. It achieved exactly what it was meant to, made by Infantino to flatter Donald Trump, the man he needed to keep on his side to safeguard the riches to be extracted from the North American market in order to consolidate his power base within Fifa. Trump, the gullible buffoon, was pleased as punch – handed a big, golden bauble and a medal he placed around his own neck – and briefly forgot about the Nobel peace prize he desperately covets . Leander Schaerlaeckens is the author of The Long Game: US Men’s Soccer and Its Savage, Four-Decade Journey to the Top, or Thereabouts, which is out now . He teaches at Marist University. Now he had the dream move lined up to Arsenal but it could not happen without breaking some hearts at Newcastle. Guimarães admits he lay awake at night as the emotions swirled. How could he leave Newcastle, the club where he made so many connections and enjoyed so many highs after joining from Lyon in January 2022 ? There were the Champions League qualifications and, above all, the Carabao Cup triumph in 2025 that ended a 70-year wait for a domestic trophy. On the other hand, how could he resist Arsenal and the prospect of competing regularly for the game’s top honours? Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
